markers.title: Nobody measured whether she turns up
markers.finding: Two moments had no data at all. Nobody measured whether a hired crew member turned up to their first shift, and nobody measured retention at ninety days.
markers.decision: The screen exists because the moment does. It is the first thing in the service built specifically for the first shift rather than for the paperwork before it, and the confirmation it asks for is the intent to turn up; attendance is recorded when the manager clocks the new starter in.
markers.rejected: Treating the offer as the end of hiring, which is what produced two moments with no owner and no number.

markers.title: One name to ask for
markers.finding: New starters arrived at the back door, or asked for whoever was on the roster, and the first ten minutes set the tone for the ninety days nobody was measuring.
markers.decision: One name, one door, one time. Arriving ten minutes early is stated as paid, because a sixteen year old will otherwise arrive at four exactly.
markers.rejected: A welcome pack, which is read by nobody on the way to a first shift.

markers.title: What to bring is almost nothing
markers.finding: Candidates brought documents they had already sent, because nothing told them the paperwork was finished.
markers.decision: Two lines: shoes, and nothing else. The second line exists to close the loop on the documents sent three days earlier.
markers.rejected: A checklist of everything that might conceivably be needed, which is how a person ends up carrying a folder to a shift.
